sections.preamble: You answer questions about a single medical image. Follow the answer format requested in the user message exactly.

content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a fibrous soft-tissue tumor.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

The large, well-circumscribed, homogeneous intermediate-signal mass lies on the image right (patient left) of the abdomen, in the area bounded by the dark rim. It spans roughly x=385–560 and y=300–520 in the left panel. In the right panel, which is offset by 784 px, that corresponds to x≈1170–1345.

Marks inside this region include 216, 196, 175, 205, 174, 203, 191, 201, and 188.

The mass centre is roughly x=1250, y=410 in the right panel. Mark 205 at (1229, 428) is the closest to that centre, and mark 175 at (1229, 368) is slightly farther away.

Mark 205 sits well within the mass and near its centre.

ANSWER: 205
